sources: Cornell Lab of Ornithology and American Bird Conservancy guidance on backyard habitat (water, cover, windows)
Xerces Society guidance on leaving leaf litter and stems
note: Free actions first. months lists the months the action makes sense (1 = January).

actions.title: Add a water source
actions.body: A shallow dish works. Refill it every few days.

actions.title: Keep some leaf cover
actions.body: Leave fallen leaves under your shrubs through winter. Insects shelter there, and birds feed on them in spring.

actions.title: Plant a native shrub
actions.body: A native shrub, like American holly, gives birds food and cover for years.

actions.title: Leave the seed heads standing
actions.body: Skip the fall cutback. Coneflower and black-eyed Susan seeds feed finches through winter.

actions.title: Scrub the birdbath weekly
actions.body: Rinse and refill it at least once a week, and daily in hot weather, so the water stays clean.

actions.title: Make a brush pile
actions.body: Stack fallen branches in a quiet corner. Small birds use it for cover.

actions.title: Skip the insect spray
actions.body: Birds feed insects to their chicks. Avoid spraying where birds nest and feed.

actions.title: Put up a nest box
actions.body: Chickadees, titmice and wrens nest in boxes. Pick a box made for the bird you want, mount it on a pole with a predator guard, and clean it out after the season.

actions.title: Leave a dead tree or branch standing
actions.body: If a dead tree or big limb is not a danger to people or buildings, leave it. Woodpeckers and nuthatches feed and nest in dead wood.

actions.title: Make windows visible
actions.body: Birds crash into reflections. Window decals or tape in a close grid help them see the glass.
